actions.reason: C0001 has coherent, strong biological identity evidence (30/50 HALLMARK pathways significant with large effects; ccRCC-relevant CNV loci) and directionally consistent cross-modal membership support with no reproducible internal subdivision or insufficient separation from other sets. Site/scanner confounding is flagged, but the defining RNA/CNV signal is not directly attributable to these technical factors, so the candidate remains defensible for downstream validation with this caveat noted.

C0002 shows mutually reinforcing RNA (immune/inflammatory downregulation) and CNV (low genomic instability, absent CDKN2A/9p/9q/14q losses) identity evidence, the most stable fused internal structure among sets (ARI 0.82), no set-specific technical confounding, and no reproducible subdivision or insufficient pairwise separation. It is a defensible discovery-stage candidate.

C0003 lacks FDR-significant RNA or CNV findings and shows discordant cross-modal membership support (only WSI positive, one zero-support patient), but there is no positive structural evidence for split or merge and no supported technical confounder. It is retained as a weak but not contradicted discovery-stage candidate with uncertainty noted.

C0004 has only weak, partially coherent biological evidence (isolated chr10q/PTEN CNV signal not reinforced by RNA or loss frequency) and strong site/CT acquisition confounding, but no positive structural evidence supports split or merge and the candidate is not actively contradicted. It is retained with substantial uncertainty for downstream validation.

C0005 lacks FDR-significant RNA or CNV findings and has weak fused internal structure, but shows the most consistent cross-modal membership support (no zero/one-support patients) and no supported technical confounder. With no positive structural evidence for split or merge, it is retained as a weak discovery-stage candidate with uncertainty noted.
